Swamishri was moving along in his wheelchair. On the way he also met Jayantibhai Sangani, who had come from America. His young son was sitting right beside him, eager for Swamishri's blessings too. He had been late yesterday, so today in his excitement he got up at half past two at night, bathed and reached the mandir early in the morning. Today, as Swamishri met everyone, he moved on without placing his hand on the boy's head, and the little boy began to sob. After giving darshan to the devotees, when Swamishri reached the lift, his eyes fell on the crying boy. Swamishri called him close and asked why he was crying, and realised he had missed placing his hand on his head. Swamishri called him near, stroked his head with a father's love, gave him a rose and had him say 'Jay Swaminarayan'.

The Vasant Panchmi celebration assembly theme was agna, upasana, sadbhav and paksh . Ishwarcharan Swami, Viveksagar Swami, Dr Swami and Mahant Swami discoursed on the four subjects. On Swamishri’s arrival a traditional dance by youths and a procession of the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj were performed and carried out. Swamishri inaugurated two publications: Ham Pahachane by Aksharjivan Swami and Shatanand Muni’s Hari Gita . After the garlanding ceremony Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Shastriji Maharaj spread the mission of Shriji Maharaj. Yogiji Maharaj fostered it and today through their wishes it has spread in India and abroad. Many types of work are done in the world, but those that please God are of honour to us. Worldly celebrations are for entertainment and joy but they do not bring peace to our soul. For inner peace one must take refuge in God and offer devotion to God. The more we imbibe the knowledge given by God the more we experience peace within…”
God’s Strength in Difficult times

28 January 2009, Vadodara An aspirant was depressed because he was hard hit by the prevailing economic recession. He came with suicidal thoughts to seek Swamishri’s blessings. Swamishri responded, “What will you do after you die! In this world one has to face difficulties and dire problems. Draw strength from God and have patience. You’ll get a solution. One who shirks from responsibility is a coward. Have patience and be brave while offering prayers. God will help you and remedy your situation.”

ds.t: Let go of him and hold on to God
w: As Swamishri goes from his residence to puja, young and old alike keep trying to catch his eye along the way. In some places children, youths or devotees also put on small presentations. These little stops sometimes become a source of inspiration. Today, as Swamishri was going towards the Nilkanth Varni Abhishek Mandap, the children had set up stops at various places for the Parents' Day being celebrated here. These stops showed the ill feeling between father and son, or the generation gap.

At one such stop a father was glued to his cell phone. His sons, standing on either side, were pleading, "Father! Make time for us." And the father angrily shooed them away. This scene was going on when Swamishri arrived, and many devotees were gathered around too. Gnanvir Swami was introducing one of them to Swamishri, but Swamishri, half listening, turned to the children acting and said, "What does your father say, does he refuse? Then let go of him now and hold on to God."

When Swamishri passes, thousands of devotees surge forward for darshan, and some also have to be introduced. Even amid all these busy moments, Swamishri heard the child's feeling, and dropped other things to give time to the child.
Swamishri was giving the message that, amid the busiest activity, every mother and father should learn to listen to their child's voice, to accept their pleading and to hear them.
